title.narrative: Output 5.3. Increased capacity of Member States to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative: The Government of South Africa adopted a National Apprenticeship and Artisan Development Strategy 2030, which was gazetted in July 2022. In May 2023, the Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET) adopted regulations for the establishment of the National Apprenticeship and Artisan Development Advisory Body (NAADAB), as a legal body for Apprenticeship and Artisan Development consultation in South Africa. Both the National Apprenticeship and Artisan Development Strategy 2030, and the Advisory Body regulations were informed by an extensive country level research and dialogue process, led by DHET and which happened in parallel to the ILO’s standard setting process on quality apprenticeship. The country level research undertaken under the auspices of the ILO’s Apprenticeship Development for Universal Lifelong Learning and Training (ADULT) and a series of country level dialogues were organised with the scope of both exposing South African constituents to the content of the ILO’s standard and to position the South Africa as a good practice in quality apprenticeship. The current national Strategy, and the tripartite constituency of the NAADAB reflect the principles of ILO’s Recommendation 208 and draw from the findings and recommendations of the ADULT research. From (Month Year) to (Month Year), and with the support from the Government of Flanders, the ILO commissioned a research study on Good practices in Apprenticeships in South-Africa, carried out jointly with the Quality Council for Trade and Occupations QCTO as lead convener, the Department of Higher Education and Training DHET (TVET Branch and Skills Branch and the National Artisan Development Advisory Body (NAADAB), which includes organised business, organised labour, government, and youth development entities (currently renamed as NAADAB). The findings of the research were shared through a series of dialogues implemented in the course of 2022(MONTHS STILL TO BE SPECIFIED) jointly convened by the DHET and the ILO, and with the active participation of the tripartite constituents and communities, through National Economic Development and Labour Advisory Council (NEDLAC).
